title: Credit Ruling: Recent Load Growth and the Reinstatement Basis Bill for Security Deposits
content:
**Applies to:** the reinstatement basis bill of a Security Deposits deposit reinstated on the waiver reinstatement basis.

## Ruling

The reinstatement basis bill follows the account's recent load. The recent average is the average bill of the three billing periods immediately before today: the usage lines billed on the Electric Service by Rate Schedule account in the three months before today, added together and divided by the number of facility charge lines billed in those months. It is compared with the window average, the average bill of the reinstatement's averaging window.

- When the recent average exceeds the window average by more than the high growth ratio of **1.35** — that is, when it is more than 1.35 times the window average — the basis bill is the recent average.
- When it is more than **1.15** times the window average but not more than 1.35 times it, the basis bill is the midpoint of the recent average and the window average: the two added together and halved.
- Otherwise the basis bill is the window average.

## Bands (hypothetical window average of $200.00)

| Recent average | Ratio to the window average | Basis bill |
|---|---|---|
| $280.00 | 1.40 | $280.00, the recent average |
| $270.00 | exactly 1.35 | $235.00, the midpoint |
| $240.00 | 1.20 | $220.00, the midpoint |
| $230.00 | exactly 1.15 | $200.00, the window average |

At exactly 1.35 times the window average the recent average does not exceed the high ratio, and at exactly 1.15 times it does not exceed the mid ratio.
